reviews.review:
I played this game for just under an hour and had to attend therapy sessions for the next 6 months 

4/10
Almost 1.5k hours in and I just learned you can backflip to stop volt's speed.

When i first stumbled over Warframe, i only read something about Ninjas and Space. It sounded cool to me so i gave it a try. 

Boy was i surprised!

Before i give you a little more text i sum up the pros and cons. Starting with cons.

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]

- You are "forced" to use a lot of different equipment (Warframes, Weapons, Companions) to increase your Mastery Rank. 
This is actually not that bad since mastery rank isn't that important. You unlock a few things with it, mostly weapons, but if you like to try a lot of different equipment you'll get the MR anyway. 

- Gameplay is a bit repetitive. Basically everything comes down to slay enemies. Lots of them. In Style. Is this really a con?

- Items in the in-game-market are pretty expensive. But there's also the trade channel, where you can get better stuff cheaper. 


[b][u]Pros:[/u][/b]

- There are very few things in the game where you "have to" spend real money for. Most notably to increase space in inventory for warframes and weapons (no space limit for ressources though). The prices for these are pretty low however and it's totaly ok. I put the "have to" in brackets because the basic space is sufficient if you only play every now and then. 

- No Pay 2 Win! If you invest money in the game you will only get things faster but they won't be better. You can get everything in the game just by playing it, besides some decorations and the afore mentioned inventory space. 

- The best equipment can not be bought in the ingame-market but has to be acquired by playing higher level missions. It can, however, be bought from other players. This is also a possible way to get your hands on the real-money-currency, platinum, without spending real money. Pretty cool. 

- Fantastic customization options, both visual and technicaly. You can paint your warframes, companions, and weapons and also attach decorational armor on them (which costs real money, but has no effect besides looks). You can even chose different animation sets for your character! There are hundreds of so called mods to improve the stats of your equipment to customize it so it suits your needs. 

- Tons of weapons! There's everything from heavy machine guns to assault rifles, shotguns, pistols, shurikens, bows and xbows, sniper rifles, swords, hammers, axes, whips (!), flame throwers, grenade launchers... you name it! I have never seen a game with so many different weapons in it. 

- Style! The animations are excellent and there's a wide variation of moves you can do, like wall-walking, somersaulting, sliding, you can equip different stance mods on melee-weapons to change the way you swing them, there are melee-combos, you can dismember enemies, pin them to walls, throw them in the air... Best thing about this is that despite the complex possibilities the controls are very accurate and easy to handle. 

- A lot of good ideas have slipped into the game, for example the way clans are handled (You build a large space station with your clan, the so called dojo, whose interior is fully customizable as well, there's support for different sizes of clans and so on)  or the fact that your base of operations is a speaking spaceship which is a bit mental . 

- The game is free!!1


To finish my little review let me say that warframe is not only one of the best f2p-games i've ever seen but it can hold it's ground against full prize games with ease. 

If you don't have it yet, get it, it's free damnit!

When I was younger I made a negative review on it. This was because at the time despite the amount of stuff to do it didn't seem to have anything coherent. However this game has changed a lot since then. Its a grind but its so worth it from beginning to end.

This space ninja farming simulator has ruined my life.

10/10.
